summary.headline: Duroply Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to Rs 122.2 crore, its highest quarter yet, with EBITDA margin up to 7.1%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter to date, with revenue of Rs 122.2 crore, up 17% YoY and 22.7% QoQ, and management said it delivered on its Q1 guidance of double-digit growth. PBT rose about 82% YoY to Rs 4.86 crore, and EBITDA rose 33.4% YoY to Rs 8.62 crore with margin at 7.1%. Gross margin dipped slightly to 34.6% on higher raw material costs. Working capital improved, with debtor days at 38 and inventory days at 151 versus the prior-year comparison. Management also launched an MDF/HGMR product on an asset-light basis.

segments.name: In-house manufactured goods
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 62.7 crore in Q2, up 18.5% YoY and 22% QoQ. H1 prior-year base stated as Rs 114 crore.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 59.5 crore in Q2, up 15.4% YoY and 23% QoQ. H1 prior-year base stated as Rs 127.8 crore.

segments.name: MDF / HGMR (new category)
segments.commentary: Launched Gero HGMR on an asset-light, leased-capacity model with no company capex; management described the start as small, with response in line with expectations. Focus is high-density retail product line.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit revenue growth in FY27 and said the second half should be better than the first half.
Management expects the current margin level to be repeatable over the next six months if raw material and freight costs do not rise further.
Management flagged risks in Delhi and NCR from construction restrictions during the winter season.
Brand spend will be kept disciplined, with returns tracked.
capex_capacity: Modernisation of the Rajpoot plant is progressing well; no capex figure or commissioning date was given.
MDF/HGMR entry is on an asset-light model using another company's capacity, with no capital outlay by Duroply.
No further MDF product extensions are planned yet; management will evaluate after establishing the current high-density line.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth was driven by higher volumes over flat overheads; COGS was similar to last year, with a minor dip in gross margin from raw material inflation.
Management said it is hard to pass on raw material cost increases to customers; shipping and chemical costs are still rising.
Competitive context: larger MDF peers struggled in Q2 with industry overcapacity, which created the opening for Duroply's entry.
Q1 was described as a blip due to challenges in April and May.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 7.1% EBITDA margin this quarter, and is it sustainable over the next two quarters and into next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin growth came from higher revenue with flat overheads, while COGS was similar to last year. It expects the performance to be repeatable over the next six months, provided raw material and shipping costs do not keep rising.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company enter MDF now, given earlier comments that no new segments were planned for 12 to 18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an asset-light opportunity arose because larger MDF peers are struggling with overcapacity and weak sales effort. It cited the brand's strength in North India and a gap in the product mix used on target construction sites. It is focusing on the high-density line and will decide on extensions later.

risks_watch: Raw material and freight cost inflation, which management says is not yet passed through to customers and may compress gross margin.
Winter construction restrictions in Delhi and NCR could affect H2 volumes.
Early-stage HGMR/MDF launch relies on a third-party's capacity; its scale and margin contribution are still unproven.
Gross margin fell to 34.6% from 35.5% in Q1; sustainability is uncertain.
Employee cost and brand spend trajectory should be watched as brand investment has increased over the last two quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and on delivering the H2 growth outlook, but cautious on raw material and freight cost uncertainty, which management says it cannot yet pass on. Responses on margin sustainability were conditional rather than firm.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 was the strongest quarter so far.
In Q1, we had given the guidance that we expected growth to move into double digits in the second quarter and we have delivered on that.
The challenge really right now is there's way too much uncertainty on the raw material cost.
So Jojo, our entry into this segment is on an asset-like model. There is no capital from the company.

adds.what: Rajpoot plant modernisation (no capex figure or commissioning date given)

growth.why: Management is "very optimistic" of double-digit FY27 revenue growth and says H2 should beat H1, but the only backing given is Q2 volume momentum, a small asset-light Gero HGMR launch on leased capacity, and competitor overcapacity; no capacity, order or contract numbers were quoted, and the Rajpoot modernisation has no capex or timing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 7.1% from 6.2% a year ago and 4.8% in Q1 on flat overheads, but management says it is conditional on raw material and freight costs not rising further, and gross margin slipped to 34.6% from 35.5% in Q1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity commissioning with a date was given; the only capacity item is the Rajpoot modernisation with no capex figure or commissioning date, and the MDF/HGMR entry uses leased third-party capacity with no capital outlay.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose 17% YoY to Rs 122.2 crore on higher volumes over flat overheads, management guided double-digit FY27 growth and said H2 should beat H1, though winter construction curbs in Delhi NCR are a risk.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed as a new program; the Rajpoot modernisation has no figure, and the MDF entry is asset-light with no company capex, so utilisation was not quoted to justify a new announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only held its double-digit FY27 growth view and called the margin repeatable conditionally, with cost inflation not yet passed through to customers, so no raise was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material and freight costs are still rising and not passed on to customers, and Delhi NCR winter construction restrictions could hit H2 volumes, though H1 revenue of Rs 221.9 crore (+12% YoY) supports the double-digit target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gero HGMR was launched in Q2 on an asset-light leased-capacity model with response in line with expectations, but management says the start is small and further MDF extensions are not yet planned.

rows.label: Competitor overcapacity opens share gains in MDF
rows.why: Larger MDF peers are struggling with industry overcapacity and weak sales effort, which management cited as the opening for Duroply's entry, but no order or share numbers were given.

rows.label: Cash conversion cycle improvement
rows.why: Debtor days fell to 38 from 42 in FY26, inventory days to 151 from 164 in Q1, and creditor days rose to 88 from 72, bringing the cash conversion cycle to 101 days.

rows.label: Brand spend and employee cost discipline
rows.why: Employee costs fell to about 10.4% of sales from 12.8% in Q1 and brand spend to 3.6% from 3.9%, but brand spend is still up from 2.7% last year and management says it will track returns.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 results, the double-digit FY27 target and H2 outlook, but cautious on raw material and freight costs it cannot yet pass on; analysts pressed on margin sustainability and on why MDF entry came earlier than the stated 12-18 month no-new-segment view.
